summary: Chinese compares with word order, not with endings like '-er'. The frame is A 比 B + adjective, and the adjective stays bare: how much more goes AFTER it (高一点儿, 高得多, 高三厘米), never 很 before it. 'Less than' is A 没有 B + adjective, 'the same' is A 跟 B 一样, and 更, 最, 比较 and 越来越 are adverbs that sit right before the adjective.

subs.label: A 比 B + adjective (no 很)
subs.focus: The learner must build A 比 B + bare adjective and decide what may stand before the adjective: nothing, 更 or 还, but not 很, 非常, 太, 真 or 比较 (有点儿 is colloquial there: never judge-wrong). Also the order: 比 B comes before the adjective, not after it as in English. Classic mistakes: 他比我很高; 他高比我.

subs.label: How much more: 一点儿, 得多, 多了, numbers
subs.focus: The learner must put the size of the difference after the adjective: 一点儿 / 一些 for a little, 得多 / 多了 for a lot, or number + measure (大两岁, 高三厘米, 贵五十块). Classic mistakes: 比他一点儿高, 比他很高 for 'much taller', and the amount before the adjective (比我两岁大).

subs.label: A 没有 B (那么) + adjective
subs.focus: The learner must say 'not as ... as' with A 没有 B (这么/那么) + adjective, not by negating the adjective inside a 比 sentence, and must keep the adjective free of amounts and degree words. Classic mistakes: 我比他不高; 我没有他高得多; 我没有他很高.

subs.label: 不比 and 不如
subs.focus: The learner must tell 不比 (not more than: maybe equal, usually contradicting someone) from 没有 and 不如 (clearly less), and build A 不如 B (+ positive adjective). Classic mistakes: 不比 used for 'less than'; 很 after 不如 (不如他很高; 不如他差 is odd, not impossible); 不如 combined with 比.

subs.label: A 跟/和 B 一样 (+ adjective), 不一样
subs.focus: The learner must express equality with A 跟/和 B 一样 (+ adjective) and difference with 不一样, choosing 跟/和 and not 比, and keeping 很 out of 一样 + adjective. Classic mistakes: 我比他一样高; 我一样高跟他. 一样很高 is said loosely: never judge-wrong.

subs.label: 最, 更 and 比较 as adverbs
subs.focus: The learner must choose 最 (top of a group), 更 (even more) or 比较 (fairly; no B named) and place it right before the adjective or 喜欢. Classic mistakes: 比较 as 'than' (这个比较那个贵); 比较 inside a 比 sentence (他比我比较高); English order with 最 (他是最高在我们班).

subs.label: 比 with verb + 得 + adjective
subs.focus: The learner must compare how an action is done: 他比我跑得快 or 他跑得比我快, keeping 得 and, when there is an object, repeating the verb or fronting the object (他说汉语说得比我好). Classic mistakes: dropping 得 (他比我跑快); 比我 after the adjective (他跑得快比我); object between verb and 得 (他说汉语得比我好).

subs.label: 越来越 + adjective
subs.focus: The learner must put 越来越 after the subject and directly before an adjective or a verb of feeling, with no other degree word, and with an action verb must attach it to the complement (跑得越来越快). Classic mistakes: 越来越很冷; 越来越更好; 越来越天气冷; 他越来越跑得快 or 他越来越跑快.

rules.rule: To say A is more ... than B, put 比 B between A and the adjective. The adjective is bare: no 很, 非常, 太 or 真 in front of it.

examples.py: jīn tiān bǐ zuó tiān lěng
examples.en: Today is colder than yesterday.

examples.py: wǒ gē ge bǐ wǒ gāo
examples.en: My older brother is taller than me.

examples.py: zhè jiàn yī fu bǐ nà jiàn guì
examples.en: This piece of clothing is more expensive than that one.

rules.note: The repeated noun in B is usually dropped: 那件, 你的, 昨天的.

rules.rule: The only degree adverbs allowed before the adjective in a 比 sentence are 更 and 还. Both mean 'even more' and imply that B is already quite tall, cold, expensive and so on.
rules.pattern: A + 比 + B + 更 / 还 + Adjective

examples.zh: 他很高，他弟弟比他更高。
examples.py: tā hěn gāo tā dì di bǐ tā gèng gāo
examples.en: He is tall, and his younger brother is even taller than him.

examples.py: jīn tiān bǐ zuó tiān hái lěng
examples.en: Today is even colder than yesterday.

examples.zh: 上海的夏天比北京更热。
examples.py: shàng hǎi de xià tiān bǐ běi jīng gèng rè
examples.en: Summer in Shanghai is even hotter than in Beijing.

rules.rule: A little more or a lot more is said after the adjective: 一点儿 or 一些 for a small difference, 得多 or 多了 for a big one.
rules.pattern: A + 比 + B + Adjective + 一点儿 / 一些 / 得多 / 多了

examples.zh: 这个比那个便宜一点儿。
examples.py: zhè ge bǐ nà ge pián yi yī diǎn r
examples.en: This one is a bit cheaper than that one.

examples.zh: 坐地铁比坐公共汽车快得多。
examples.py: zuò dì tiě bǐ zuò gōng gòng qì chē kuài de duō
examples.en: Taking the subway is much faster than taking the bus.

examples.py: tā de hàn yǔ bǐ wǒ hǎo duō le
examples.en: His Chinese is much better than mine.

rules.note: 有点儿 before the adjective is not standard in a 比 sentence (比昨天有点儿冷 is heard in speech); use 一点儿 after the adjective. 得多 and 多了 are interchangeable here. In speech 很多 after the adjective (贵很多) is also heard; 很 before the adjective is never possible.

rules.rule: An exact difference is number + measure word, and it also goes after the adjective. For ages use 大 and 小.
rules.pattern: A + 比 + B + Adjective + number + measure

examples.py: wǒ jiě jie bǐ wǒ dà liǎng suì
examples.en: My older sister is two years older than me.

examples.py: tā bǐ wǒ gāo sān lí mǐ
examples.en: He is three centimetres taller than me.

examples.py: zhè jiàn bǐ nà jiàn guì wǔ shí kuài
examples.en: This one is fifty yuan more expensive than that one.

rules.rule: 'A is not as ... as B' is A 没有 B + adjective, often with 这么 or 那么 before the adjective. Do not negate the adjective in a 比 sentence, and do not add amounts or 得多 after the adjective.
rules.pattern: A + 没有 + B + (这么 / 那么) + Adjective

examples.py: wǒ méi yǒu tā gāo
examples.en: I'm not as tall as he is.

examples.py: jīn tiān méi yǒu zuó tiān nà me lěng
examples.en: Today is not as cold as yesterday.

examples.py: zuò huǒ chē méi yǒu zuò fēi jī kuài
examples.en: Taking the train is not as fast as flying.

rules.note: The adjective is normally the 'big' end of the scale (高, 大, 快, 贵, 好). 没 alone (我没他高) is common in speech.

rules.rule: A 不比 B + adjective means 'A is not more ... than B': they may be about the same. It is mostly used to disagree with what someone said or expects. For a plain 'less than', use 没有.

examples.zh: 他不比我高，我们差不多。
examples.py: tā bù bǐ wǒ gāo wǒ men chà bu duō
examples.en: He's no taller than me; we're about the same.

examples.zh: 这家店的东西不比那家便宜。
examples.py: zhè jiā diàn de dōng xi bù bǐ nà jiā pián yi
examples.en: Things in this shop are no cheaper than in that one.

rules.note: 不 goes before 比, never before the adjective: 比我不高 is wrong.

rules.rule: A 不如 B means 'A is not as good as B'. An adjective can be added to say in what way, and it normally names a good or 'big' quality. 不如 replaces 比; the two are not combined.

examples.py: wǒ de hàn yǔ bù rú tā
examples.en: My Chinese is not as good as his.

examples.zh: 这个手机不如那个好用。
examples.py: zhè ge shǒu jī bù rú nà ge hǎo yòng
examples.en: This phone is not as easy to use as that one.

examples.py: zǒu lù bù rú qí zì xíng chē kuài
examples.en: Walking is not as fast as riding a bike.

rules.note: 不如 is a little more formal than 没有. Without an adjective, 没有 cannot replace it: 我的汉语没有他 is incomplete.

rules.rule: 'The same as' is A 跟 B 一样 or A 和 B 一样, and an adjective can follow 一样 with no 很. 'Different' is 不一样. 比 is never used with 一样.
rules.pattern: A + 跟 / 和 + B + 一样 / 不一样 + (Adjective)

examples.py: wǒ gēn tā yī yàng gāo
examples.en: I'm as tall as he is.

examples.py: wǒ de shǒu jī hé nǐ de yī yàng
examples.en: My phone is the same as yours.

examples.zh: 这两个字的意思不一样。
examples.py: zhè liǎng ge zì de yì si bù yī yàng
examples.en: The meanings of these two characters are different.

examples.zh: 这里的冬天跟北京一样冷。
examples.py: zhè lǐ de dōng tiān gēn běi jīng yī yàng lěng
examples.en: Winter here is as cold as in Beijing.

rules.note: 不一样 usually stands alone, without an adjective. 一样很贵 is heard in loose speech; the standard form has no 很. To say 'not as tall as', use 没有 (我没有他高) rather than 跟他不一样高.

rules.rule: 最 marks the top of a group of three or more; 更 means 'even more' than something just mentioned. Both go directly before the adjective or a verb such as 喜欢. The group goes before 最, not after it.
rules.pattern: (Group) + 最 / 更 + Adjective / 喜欢 ...

examples.py: tā shì wǒ men bān zuì gāo de
examples.en: He is the tallest in our class.

examples.py: wǒ zuì xǐ huan chūn tiān
examples.en: I like spring best.

examples.py: zhè ge bù cuò nà ge gèng hǎo
examples.en: This one is good; that one is even better.

rules.rule: 比较 before an adjective is an adverb meaning 'fairly, rather'. No B is named. It is not the 比 of comparison and cannot be put into a 比 sentence.
rules.pattern: Subject + 比较 + Adjective / 喜欢 ...

examples.py: jīn tiān bǐ jiào lěng
examples.en: It's fairly cold today.

examples.py: zhè ge wèn tí bǐ jiào nán
examples.en: This question is rather difficult.

examples.py: wǒ bǐ jiào xǐ huan hē chá
examples.en: I prefer drinking tea.

rules.rule: To compare how an action is done, keep verb + 得 + adjective and put 比 B either before the verb or right after 得. With an object, repeat the verb or put the object first.
rules.pattern: A + 比 + B + Verb + 得 + Adjective  /  A + Verb + 得 + 比 + B + Adjective

examples.py: tā bǐ wǒ pǎo de kuài
examples.en: He runs faster than me.

examples.py: tā pǎo de bǐ wǒ kuài
examples.en: He runs faster than me.

examples.py: mèi mei chàng gē chàng de bǐ wǒ hǎo
examples.en: My younger sister sings better than I do.

examples.py: wǒ jīn tiān bǐ zuó tiān qǐ de zǎo
examples.en: I got up earlier today than yesterday.

rules.note: Both positions of 比 B are correct and mean the same. Amounts still go at the very end: 他跑得比我快得多. The negative uses 没有 in the same slots: 我跑得没有他快.

rules.rule: 'More and more' is 越来越 right before an adjective or a verb of feeling, after the subject, usually with 了 at the end. No 很 or 更 with it. With an action verb, 越来越 goes after 得.
rules.pattern: Subject + 越来越 + Adjective + (了)  /  Subject + Verb + 得 + 越来越 + Adjective

examples.py: tiān qì yuè lái yuè lěng le
examples.en: The weather is getting colder and colder.

examples.zh: 我越来越喜欢这个城市了。
examples.py: wǒ yuè lái yuè xǐ huan zhè ge chéng shì le
examples.en: I like this city more and more.

examples.zh: 他汉语说得越来越好了。
examples.py: tā hàn yǔ shuō de yuè lái yuè hǎo le
examples.en: He speaks Chinese better and better.

right.py: tā bǐ wǒ gāo de duō
right.en: He is much taller than me.

contrasts.why: 很 cannot stand before the adjective in a 比 sentence. 'Much' is said after the adjective with 得多 or 多了.

right.py: jīn tiān bǐ zuó tiān lěng yī diǎn r
right.en: Today is a bit colder than yesterday.

contrasts.why: The amount of difference goes after the adjective: 冷一点儿. (比昨天有点儿冷 is heard in casual speech, but adjective + 一点儿 is the standard form.)

right.py: wǒ bǐ jiě jie xiǎo liǎng suì
right.en: I'm two years younger than my older sister.

contrasts.why: English says 'two years younger'; Chinese puts the number after the adjective.

right.en: I'm not as tall as he is.

contrasts.why: A 比 sentence is not negated at the adjective. 'Not as tall as' is A 没有 B 高.

right.py: wǒ méi yǒu tā nà me gāo
right.en: I'm not as tall as he is.

contrasts.why: After 没有 the adjective takes no amount or degree complement; only 这么 or 那么 may come before it.

right.py: wǒ gēn tā yī yàng gāo
right.en: I'm as tall as he is.

contrasts.why: 比 always means a difference. Sameness uses 跟 or 和 with 一样.

right.py: tā bǐ wǒ pǎo de kuài

contrasts.why: Describing how an action is done needs 得 between the verb and the adjective, in a comparison too.

right.py: zhè ge bǐ nà ge guì
right.en: This one is more expensive than that one.

contrasts.why: 比较 before an adjective means 'fairly' and takes no B. 'Than' is 比 alone.

right.py: tā shì wǒ men bān zuì gāo de
right.en: He is the tallest in our class.

contrasts.why: The group goes before 最, not after it as in English 'tallest in our class'.

right.py: tiān qì yuè lái yuè lěng le
right.en: The weather is getting colder and colder.

contrasts.why: 越来越 already gives the degree, so 很, 更 and 非常 cannot be added. 了 at the end marks the change.

cheat: 比 in the sentence? Adjective bare: no 很, 非常, 太, 有点儿. Only 更 or 还 may stand before it.
How much more goes AFTER the adjective: 高一点儿, 高得多, 高多了, 高三厘米, 大两岁.
'Not as ... as' = A 没有 B (那么) + adjective. Never 比 ... 不 + adjective.
不比 = 'no more than' (maybe equal); 不如 = 'not as good as', normally with a positive adjective.
Same = 跟 / 和 ... 一样 (+ adjective), different = 不一样. No 比, no 很.
Action compared? Keep 得: 比我跑得快 or 跑得比我快.
越来越 and 比较 sit right before the adjective, alone: no 很, no 更, no B.
